title: Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition & Billing (Q3 2026)
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core Finance & Legal operating procedures for: budgeting & forecasting, procurement and purchase approvals, contract lifecycle and legal review, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product and engineering managers who participate in planning, vendor onboarding, or commercial contract execution.

Scope
- Applies to all legal entities where Redwood Inference books revenue and incur expenses.
- Covers: annual budget and rolling forecast cadence, procurement thresholds and approval workflow, contract review checklist and standard clauses, revenue recognition rules and billing cadence.
- Does not replace entity-specific tax or audit guidance; consult Finance for cross-border or complex tax questions.

Owners & RACI
- Budget owner: VP Finance (owner)
- Forecasting coordinator: FP&A Manager (accountable)
- Procurement approvals: Procurement Lead (responsible), Requesting manager (initiator), Legal (consulted for contract review), Engineering/Product (consulted for technical fit), CFO (approver for >$500k)
- Contract review and signing: Legal (owner), Commercial lead (R), Finance (C for revenue terms), CEO/CFO (A for large strategic deals)

Budgeting & Forecasting Process
1) Annual planning (timeline)
   - Apr–May: Strategic planning & headcount planning (Product & Eng inputs).
   - Jun: Finance consolidates departmental budgets; leadership reviews.
   - Jul: Finalize board-facing budget; publish internal budgets and targets.
2) Rolling forecast (monthly)
   - Rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly by FP&A. Variance analysis due by 5th business day.
3) Approval gates and thresholds
   - Department-level re-allocations up to $50k: Department head sign-off.
   - Mid-level adjustments $50k–$250k: Department head + Finance sign-off.
   - Revisions >$250k: FP&A + CFO approval and leadership notification.

Budget categories (example table)
| Category | Owner | Budget cadence | Key validation points |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Personnel (headcount & comp) | People Ops & Dept Head | Annual + quarterly refresh | Headcount plan, offer budget, ramp assumptions |
| Cloud & Infra | Eng Infrastructure | Annual + monthly forecast | Utilization metrics, reserved commitments |
| Contracted Services & SaaS | Procurement | Quarterly refresh | Vendor contracts, termination windows |
| Capital & Hardware | Eng Infra | Annual | Depreciation schedule, procurement timeline |

Templates & artifacts
- Budget workbook (Google Sheets): /finance/templates/budget-annual-2026.
- Rolling forecast template: /finance/templates/rolling-forecast-12m.
- Headcount planning sheet: /people-ops/headcount-2026.

Procurement & Purchase Approval Flow
Procurement is centralized to ensure contract terms, security checks, and cost control. Follow this flow for all purchases > $5k.

Procurement thresholds & approval matrix
| Amount (USD) | Required approvals | Procurement involvement | Additional requirements |
|---:|---|---|---|
| <$5,000 | Requesting manager | Optional (procurement advisory) | Standard vendor onboarding OK |
| $5,000–$50,000 | Dept head + Procurement | Procurement to run vendor/vendor consolidation check | PO required; standard T&C acceptable |
| $50,000–$250,000 | Dept head + Procurement + Finance | Procurement to conduct commercial negotiation; Legal review if custom T&Cs | PO + contract redlines required |
| $250,000–$500,000 | VP (owner) + Procurement + Finance + Legal | Sourcing review; total cost of ownership assessment | CFO notified; multi-year commitments require board notice |
| >$500,000 | CFO + Procurement + Legal + CEO for strategic buys | Competitive sourcing strongly recommended; executive sign-off | Board-level reporting for multiyear/strategic commitments |

Standard procurement procedure (numbered steps)
1. Initiate purchase request via Procurement Portal (link: /tools/procurement). Include business justification, GL code, expected start/end date, and budget owner.
2. Procurement validates vendor (security questionnaire, SOC2 if applicable) and runs vendor consolidation check.
3. If procurement scope < $50k and standard T&C: procurement issues PO and records contract.
4. If custom terms or >$50k: send draft contract to Legal with vendor information and risk summary.
5. Legal reviews and produces redlines within 5 business days (priority levels expedite).
6. Once terms agreed, Finance issues PO/invoice routing instructions; procurement completes onboarding and registers vendor in ERP.

Required documentation at time of purchase
- Business justification memo (1–2 paragraphs)
- Approved PO (if >$5k)
- Signed contract or executed order form (if vendor requires)
- Vendor W-9 or tax form and bank details for payment setup
- Security/compliance evidence for vendors handling PII/production access (SOC2, AOC, or security questionnaire)

Contracts & Legal Process
Contract types covered
- Standard SaaS subscription agreements
- Professional services statements of work (SOWs)
- Reseller / channel agreements
- NDAs & MOU
- Data processing agreements (DPA) and BAA where applicable

Contract lifecycle checklist
- Intake: Complete contract intake form (link: /legal/contract-intake) and attach vendor materials.
- Risk assessment: Legal assigns a risk tier (Low/Medium/High) based on data access, indemnity, IP, and termination terms.
- Commercial review: Finance confirms revenue/cost treatment and billing terms.
- Security review: Security team sign-off for any production access or data transfer.
- Sign-off: Legal certifies final redlines; authorized signatory executes.

Standard clauses & playbook notes
- Use Redwood standard SaaS addendum for SaaS vendors where possible. Do not accept unilateral vendor indemnity or unlimited liability without Legal escalation.
- Termination: Prefer 30–90 day termination for convenience in standard contracts. Avoid auto-renew without notification.
- Data residency: Include DPA and flow-down clauses for sub-processors where required by customer/regulatory commitments.

Escalations and SLA for legal review
- Low risk: 3–5 business days
- Medium risk: 5–10 business days
- High risk / strategic: 10+ business days; set SLA with commercial team and prioritize via Legal intake.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Purpose: Ensure consistent application of ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles across the business for recognition and billing.

Revenue model categories
- Usage-based hosted API revenue (metered tokens/embeddings).
- Subscription & committed reserved (Dedicated) revenue (monthly/annual).
- Professional services and onboarding (one-time SOWs).
- Private deployment / licensing revenue (multi-year).

Recognition principles (summary)
- Identify the contract: Signed order form or agreed subscription with commercial terms.
- Identify performance obligations: e.g., access to API, model hosting, professional services deliverables.
- Determine transaction price: Fee schedules, volume discounts, credits, usage estimates.
- Allocate price to obligations: Separately account for distinct performance obligations (e.g., one-time implementation vs ongoing service).
- Recognize when satisfied: Usage revenue recognized as usage occurs; subscription revenue recognized ratably over service period; professional services recognized on completion or percentage-of-completion if measurable.

Deferred revenue examples
- Annual prepay for Dedicated capacity: record as deferred revenue and amortize monthly over the term.
- Prepaid annual support add-ons: recognize ratably.

Billing cadence & invoicing rules
- Usage-based customers: monthly invoice with usage detail; invoices issued within 5 business days after month-end. Disputed invoices must be raised within 30 days.
- Subscription customers: invoice schedule per contract (monthly or annual). Annual prepayments require PO + invoice prior to term start.
- Professional services: milestone billing aligned to SOW. Retainers recognized per contract.

Collections & credit holds
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 (unless contract specifies otherwise).
- Overdue balances >60 days: account moved to Collections team; services may be suspended after 90 days with Legal approval.

Billing system integrations and GL mapping (example)
Example GL mapping snippet (YAML):
```yaml
revenue_mappings:
  usage_api:
    gl_account: "4001"
    recognition: "usage"
  subscription_dedicated:
    gl_account: "4010"
    recognition: "ratable"
  professional_services:
    gl_account: "4020"
    recognition: "milestone"
```

Tools, templates & location of records
- ERP / AP: Netsuite (vendor and invoice master)
- Procurement portal: /tools/procurement
- Contract repository: /legal/contracts (executed PDFs stored with metadata)
- Billing & usage analytics: Billing dashboard (internal) and usage export CSV via /tools/billing-api
- Retention: Financial records stored for 7 years per policy in /finance/archive

Exceptions, Risk & Audit
- Any deviations from this playbook (e.g., expedited procurement without PO; acceptance of non-standard indemnity) must be logged as an exception and approved by Finance + Legal and recorded in /finance/exceptions register.
- Audit readiness: include contract evidences, POs, invoices, vendor tax documents and security attestations. Finance retains supporting documentation for recognized revenue and deferred balances.

Escalation paths
- Procurement dispute: Procurement Lead -> VP Finance -> CFO.
- Contract dispute: Legal Counsel -> General Counsel -> CEO.
- RevRec/billing exception: Revenue Accounting -> Finance Controller -> VP Finance.

Appendix A: Quick checklists
Budget submission checklist (for managers):
- Completed budget workbook row(s) with assumptions
- Headcount request linked to HR requisition
- Business justification and KPI alignment
- Forecast variance commentary for prior period

Procurement quick checklist (for requests >$50k):
- Completed procurement request form
- Security questionnaire if vendor accesses production
- Contract intake form completed and attached
- Budget approval evidence (email or system approval)
